name: Dominica
headline: Dominica has no data protection law, and the national health record system it has announced was still being prepared for rollout in mid-2026.

access.summary: No law gives patients a right to see or copy their health record: Dominica has no data protection act and no freedom of information act. A patient portal is planned in the national health information system, but it is not live.
detail: The US State Department's 2026 investment statement says Dominica has not enacted a comprehensive data protection policy. UWI's data protection office reported the same as at February 2025.
The Constitution protects the privacy of a person's home and other property. It does not create a right of access to records.
The government HMIS site says a patient portal will give patients secure access to their personal health records. Its own implementation table still lists both go-live phases as not yet scheduled.
No hospital or ministry policy on giving patients copies of their records was found. Access depends on each facility.

control.summary: With no data protection law, patients have no legal right to consent to or refuse sharing of their health data. The planned HMIS promises role-based access, an audit trail and patient choice over private doctors, but none of this is live.
detail: No statute requires consent before health data is used or shared. The HMIS project itself says data protection and privacy laws still need to be drafted and passed.
The HMIS FAQ says staff will see only what their role needs, mental health and infectious disease data will be highly restricted, and a patient may choose to give a private doctor access.
The FAQ also promises an audit trail recording who accessed the system, when and from where. No patient-visible access log is described.
No opt-out from record sharing was found. The score stays in the 20 to 35 band because these controls are plans, not working tools.

privacy.summary: Dominica has no data protection law, no regulator, no breach notification duty and no penalties for misusing health data. Hospital staff owe a duty of confidentiality under section 49 of the Hospitals Authority Act 2021, and a 2024 leak ended in a resignation.
detail: The 2026 US State Department statement says no comprehensive data protection policy exists; privacy rests on the Constitution, and the Electronic Evidence Act covers records used in court.

In January 2024 a hospital staff member's voice note about a patient circulated on social media. The Dominica Hospitals Authority cited section 49 confidentiality duties, began discipline, and the staff member resigned.
The ECCB published policy considerations in March 2025 for a harmonised data protection law with a regulator. No Dominican law had passed by the research date.
The general-law band of 45 to 66 does not fit here because there is no general law. The score sits below it, as for other peers without a working regulator.

commercial.summary: No law limits the sale of health data or its use for marketing, and no rules cover health apps or data brokers. The only national privacy policy found covers personal data collected on government websites.
detail: Without a data protection act, there is no purpose limit, consent rule or ban on selling personal data, including health data.
UWI notes that the government's website privacy policy promises not to share data given through official sites without consent. It does not bind private companies.
No rules on consumer health apps, data brokers or de-identified data sales were found, and no enforcement case was found.

journey.summary: A national HMIS is planned for three hospitals and 49 health centres, but in June 2026 the ministry was still preparing its rollout. The national lab runs a fully electronic information system, and surveillance uses DHIS2 alongside paper.
detail: The HMIS is being built for Dominica China Friendship Hospital, Reginald Fitzroy Armour Hospital, Marigot Hospital and 49 primary care centres.

The project's home page announces the HMIS as launched, but its own implementation table leaves both go-live phases unscheduled. In June 2026 PAHO donated 20 computers, partly to support preparations for the HMIS rollout.
The National Medical Laboratory moved its fully electronic Laboratory Information System to a new server on 25 June 2026.
A PAHO mission in May 2026 trained staff on DHIS2 for respiratory and syndromic surveillance, after a 2025 assessment found continued reliance on paper.

clinical.summary: Clinicians cannot yet see a patient's record across facilities, because the shared HMIS is not live. Lab results are electronic at the national lab, but private doctors are not linked and old paper records will not be fully migrated.
detail: The HMIS FAQ says doctors and pharmacists will see prescriptions and allergy alerts, and all lab results will appear once the system is fully implemented.
Old records will not be bulk loaded. Clinicians will decide, patient by patient, which past information to transfer.
Private doctors have resisted the system, and the FAQ says their access still awaits a policy decision.
The lab upgrade aims to speed results to emergency staff, but a link from the lab system to a shared record was not found.

research.summary: No law requires ethics approval for clinical trials, says the 2012 ministry and PAHO pharmaceutical profile, and with no data protection law nothing governs reuse of health records. A National Human Research Ethics Committee has approved studies, adding one safeguard to the base score.
detail: The 2012 Pharmaceutical Country Profile, published by the health ministry with PAHO, says no law requires authorisation for clinical trials, ethics committee agreement, or registration in a trial registry. Whether this has changed since was not found.
A 2013 peer-reviewed study of gastroenteritis in Dominica reports approval by the National Human Research Ethics Committee of Dominica.
With no data protection law, there is no consent rule, opt-out or public register for research use of health records.

ai.summary: No law, guidance or regulator covers clinical AI, and Dominica has no medicines or device regulator. Ministry staff were trained in 2026 to use AI tools such as Copilot for data work, with no published rules.
detail: The 2012 pharmaceutical profile says Dominica has no Medicines Regulatory Authority, so no body regulates software as a medical device. No later regulator was found.
In May 2026 a PAHO-supported ministry training showed clerical staff how to use AI tools, including Copilot, in Excel. No policy on AI and patient data was mentioned.
A June 2026 review by a training firm found no AI law, bill, strategy or regulator. That is a secondary source; no official AI policy was found to confirm or contradict it.

journeyNote: The national HMIS linking hospitals and 49 clinics is planned but not live. The national lab system is electronic. Surveillance uses DHIS2 with some paper. Claims systems were not verified. Not in the EU, so the EHDS does not apply.

laws.name: Constitution of the Commonwealth of Dominica
laws.what: Protects privacy of the home and other property; no general data protection or record access right.

laws.name: Dominica Hospitals Authority Act, 2021 (No. 8 of 2021), amended by Act No. 13 of 2024
laws.what: Creates the Hospitals Authority; the hospital cites its section 49 confidentiality duty for staff. Link is the 2024 amendment.

laws.name: Medical Profession Act, 2026
laws.what: Creates a Dominica Medical Council with complaints and disciplinary committees for doctors.

laws.name: Medical Laboratories Act, 2024
laws.what: Sets up a Medical Laboratories Council to license labs and staff and enforce quality standards.

laws.name: Electronic Evidence Act, 2010
laws.what: Governs electronic records as evidence in court; not a data protection law.
